messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High serving tail latency detected for /v1/responses (us-west-2). 90th=4200ms, 99th=9800ms, SSE error rate spiked to 7% in last 5m. Auto-mitigation not triggered because traffic route is mixed.

sophia: seeing a lot of queued requests on the runtime side, GPU scheduling backlog growing. charts: https://dash.redwood.example/boards/serve-latency (link)

amir: confirmed. kernel hotpath showing KV-cache thrashing + long context switch on the batching thread. Differs by model size.

leo-oncall: @sophia i'm on it, handoff 2148001120. can we isolate by tier? is dedicated affected?

sophia: dedicated pools are fine. Hosted (free/standard) is where queues are spiking. Likely PLG burst from region + a bad long-seq workload.

paul: support report inbound: a customer reported degraded streaming in us-west-2 starting ~2148000950. ticket #CS-8421. customer-success looped.

customer-success: flagged to customers in affected orgs. need ETA for mitigation before we post to status.

amir: mitigation options: 1) rate-limit streaming endpoints by token/conn 2) reduce batch size globally 3) temporally disable streaming (SSE/chunked) and fall back to poll/polling or non-streaming responses 4) scale more capacity (slow).

leo-oncall: what's the quickest with lowest blast radius?

sophia: quickest is toggling streaming feature flag for Hosted regionally (us-west-2) to stop push frames. clients will get final responses as single payloads. impacts UX but reduces connection churn and KV-cache pressure.

opsbot: RUNBOOK CHECK: /playbooks/live-mitigation -> recommended: partial disable streaming + shape traffic + raise per-user quotas temporarily.

amir: I can flip the feature flag for Hosted only. command: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://control-plane.redwood.internal/flags/streaming/disable -d '{"scope":"hosted","region":"us-west-2","reason":"latency-stabilization"}'```

leo-oncall: do it. also add a rate-limit at the edge for 1.5x current QPS to avoid sudden spikes when clients switch to polling.

paul: will tell support to prepare canned message: "We’re temporarily disabling streaming responses in us-west-2 to stabilize latency. Non-streaming responses will continue. Expected impact: up to 2x token costs for some customers, degraded immediacy for chat-like apps."

support-agent: got it. drafting update for status.redwood.ai and CS portal.

opsbot: ACTION: Applying feature-flag change (initiated by amir). Output: ```{"status":"started","op_id":"op-2148001135"}```

opsbot: FEATURE FLAG UPDATE: success. ```{"op_id":"op-2148001135","result":"disabled","scope":"hosted:us-west-2","timestamp":2148001140}```

incident-bot: NOTE: Streaming disabled for hosted/us-west-2 by amir at 2148001140. Monitoring for 10m.

sophia: initial telemetry: 5m after toggle 90th latency down to 750ms, 99th 1800ms, SSE error -> 0.6%. queue depth reduced ~68%.

amir: added edge rate-limit: ```edgectl apply --region usw2 --rule "responses: qps <= 1.5*baseline"``` returns OK.

leo-oncall: good. please keep monitoring for 30m. If stable, we'll keep disabled and schedule a gradual canary re-enable after kernel patch and adjusted batching heuristics.

paul: CS update posted to affected customers and status page. support triage to escalate any customer regressions to me.

customer-success: received one high-visibility customer reply unhappy about UX; offered 30min call and temporary refund credit.

opsbot: METRICS SNAPSHOT (2148001200): request rate -12%, token rate -8%, p50 latency -20%, p99 latency -75%, streaming connections -down 95%.

amir: next steps captured: - implement short-term batch size cap; - add connection backpressure handling in runtime; - plan a friday rollout with kernel fixes and staged streaming re-enable; - postmortem + RCA.

leo-oncall: assigning follow-ups: amir -> runtime changes, sophia -> rollout plan + canary, paul -> customer comms + billing checklist.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated (streaming disabled, edge shaping applied). Will remain open until re-enable. Closing updates will include timeline & RCA.

sophia: leaving monitoring watch for next 45m, handoff to leo at 2148001300.

leo-oncall: noted. I'll follow up on the canary and re-enable playbook once we have kernel patch and controlled load test.

paul: thanks team. postmortem owner: leo. expect draft within 48h.

support-agent: tagging #status-updates once we have ETA for re-enable. :white_check_mark:
